description: Somos TecnoNexo, un equipo de Piura con experiencia en programación, análisis de datos y ciencias aplicadas. Participamos en el reto “Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots”, con interés en desarrollar una solución basada en datos satelitales que facilite el análisis y visualización de la actividad de fuego.
summary: FirePulse is a web application that harmonizes NASA FIRMS active-fire and thermal-anomaly detections from MODIS and VIIRS into a consistent historical fire-activity record for Peru. MODIS and VIIRS observe thermal activity at different spatial resolutions and sensitivities, so their raw hotspot counts cannot be compared directly through time. FirePulse addresses this by placing detections into a common 1 km spatial grid, aggregating them by cell and day, preserving sensor-level evidence, and calibrating MODIS against VIIRS during their overlap period. Users can explore fire activity by region and date, inspect individual detections, and compare current activity with historical medians and percentiles.
details:
FirePulse is a web-based fire-intelligence platform developed to harmonize NASA FIRMS active-fire and thermal-anomaly observations from MODIS and VIIRS.

We processed 2,439,268 satellite detections from MODIS Terra/Aqua and VIIRS Suomi-NPP, NOAA-20 and NOAA-21.

How it works

1. Data ingestion and quality control

Coordinates, timestamps, FRP values, sensor information and data status are standardized while preserving traceability to the original NASA FIRMS observations.

2. Temporal normalization

Acquisition timestamps are converted into consistent temporal units for analysis.

3. Common spatial framework

MODIS and VIIRS detections are assigned to a shared 1 km × 1 km grid, allowing observations from sensors with different spatial resolutions to be analyzed within the same reference system.

4. Cell × day aggregation

The common analytical unit is one spatial cell during one day. This reduces the effect of different sensor resolutions and multiple observations of the same area.

5. Sensor evidence preservation

MODIS and VIIRS remain identifiable after harmonization. Users can inspect the original sensor, acquisition time, FRP and other attributes of individual observations.

6. Cross-sensor calibration

The overlapping MODIS–VIIRS period is used to estimate monthly calibration relationships, allowing historical MODIS activity to be expressed on a comparable VIIRS-equivalent reference scale.

7. Independent validation

Calibration and validation periods are separated to evaluate whether the harmonization performs on periods that were not used to estimate the calibration.

8. Historical context

FirePulse calculates harmonized activity, historical medians, relative anomalies and historical percentiles for selected regions and periods.

9. Interactive exploration

Users can explore Peru nationally or by department, filter observations by date, visualize MODIS and VIIRS detections, inspect sensor-level information, use an activity calendar, and compare observed activity with historical behavior.

FirePulse does not interpret every satellite hotspot as a confirmed wildfire. The platform presents NASA FIRMS observations as active-fire or thermal-anomaly detections and uses cautious labels such as probable fire type or candidate event where appropriate.
